phrases.arabic: ما قِدِرْت أرِد عَلَيْك قَبَل شْوَي
بِتِقْدِر تِرْجَع تِتَّصِل فِيني بَعِد شْوَي؟
phrases.transliteration: btid2ar tirja3 tittasil fiini ba3d shwaay?

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.english: Hello?

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.english: Hi Samer, it's Lina.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.english: Hi Lina, what's new?

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: الحمد لله تمام. اتصلت فيك قبل شوي بس كان الخط مشغول
dialogue.transliteration: il7amdella tamaam. ittasalt fiik 2abel shwaay bas kaan il-khatt mashghuul
dialogue.english: All good, thank God. I called you a bit ago but the line was busy.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: إي، كنت عم إحكي مع أخي. آسف إنو ما قدرت أرد عليك
dialogue.transliteration: ee, kint 3am i7ki ma3 akhi. aasif enno ma 2dirt radd 3aleek
dialogue.english: Yeah, I was talking with my brother. Sorry I couldn't answer you.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: ولا يهمك. بدي إحكي معك عن موضوع الموعد
dialogue.transliteration: wala yhimmak. biddi i7ki ma3ak 3an mawḍuu3 il-maw3id
dialogue.english: Don't worry about it. I want to talk to you about the appointment.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: تفضلي، بس ثانية واحدة، رصيدي عم يخلص
dialogue.transliteration: tfaḍḍali, bas saanye wa7de, rasiidi 3am yikhlas
dialogue.english: Go ahead, just a second, my credit is about to run out.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: طيب خليني أحكي بسرعة قبل ما ينقطع الخط معك
dialogue.transliteration: tayyib khalliini i7ki bsur3a 2abel ma yin2ata3 il-khatt ma3ak
dialogue.english: Okay let me talk fast before the call gets cut off on you.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: لأ لأ، خلص، انقطع. بتقدري ترجعي تتصلي فيني بعد شوي؟
dialogue.transliteration: la2 la2, khalas, in2ata3. btid2ari tirja3i tittasili fiini ba3d shwaay?
dialogue.english: No no, it's over, it got cut off. Can you call me back in a bit?

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: ماشي، منيح إنك اتصلت أصلا. بترجع أتصل فيك
dialogue.transliteration: maashi, mnii7 ennak ittasalt aslan. birja3 ittasil fiik
dialogue.english: Okay, good that you called at all. I'll call you back.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.english: Thanks, I'll wait for you.

pair.arabic: بِتِقْدِر تِرْجَع تِتَّصِل فِيني بَعِد شْوَي؟
pair.transliteration: btid2ar tirja3 tittasil fiini ba3d shwaay?
pair.english: Can you call me back in a bit?

lessons.culture: In Damascus a call usually opens with "آلو؟" rather than the caller's name, so the person answering asks "مين معي؟" to find out who it is. Ending a call abruptly without a short goodbye like "يسلمو" or "بستناك" can come across as cold.

exercises.prompt: You pick up the phone and hear: "آلو؟". Answer naturally, asking who is calling.

too_formal.item: السلام عليكم، من فضلك من المتصل؟
too_formal.feedback: This is correct Arabic, but far more formal than the ordinary way of answering the phone.

exercises.tip: "آلو؟" is the everyday way to open a call in Damascus.

exercises.prompt: A friend asks you on the phone: "شو الأخبار؟". Say that everything is fine, thank God.

too_formal.item: الأمور على ما يرام، ولله الحمد
too_formal.feedback: Correct but bookish; a spoken reply is much shorter.

exercises.tip: "الحمد لله" almost always appears somewhere in the answer.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "ما قدرت _____ عليك قبل شوي." Meaning: I couldn't answer you a bit ago.

too_formal.feedback: Understandable, but "رد" is the word actually used on the phone in Damascene speech.

exercises.tip: "رد على حدا" is the everyday phrase for answering someone's call.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "_____ الخط معي وأنا عم إحكي معك." Meaning: The call got cut off on me while I was talking to you.

too_formal.feedback: Correct but sounds like a technical report, not something a person says on the phone.

exercises.tip: "قطع الخط" or "انقطع الخط" both describe a dropped call.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Damascene Arabic: "My battery died."

too_formal.feedback: Grammatically fine, but far more formal than how people actually say it.

exercises.tip: "خلص" / "خلصت" covers running out of almost anything: credit, battery, patience.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "There's no signal here."

too_formal.item: لا توجد تغطية شبكية في هذا المكان
too_formal.feedback: Correct but reads like a technician's report, not spoken Damascene.

exercises.tip: "تغطية" is the everyday word for phone signal/coverage.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "My credit ran out"?

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but "خلص" is the word used in everyday speech, not "انتهى".

exercises.tip: "رصيد" is prepaid phone credit.

exercises.prompt: Which is the natural way to answer an incoming call?

too_formal.feedback: Too formal; nobody opens a phone call this way in Damascene speech.

exercises.tip: "آلو" answers the phone; the other phrases come once the call is already going.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "مشغول / كان / الخط".

too_formal.feedback: That would be an unusual, technical way to say the line was busy.

exercises.tip: Subject "الخط" comes right after "كان" here.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "فيني / بعد شوي / ترجع / تتصل".

too_formal.item: هل بإمكانك معاودة الاتصال بي لاحقاً
too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but this is the formal written version, not the spoken order of words.

exercises.tip: "ترجع" + verb is how Damascene speech says "do it again": "ترجع تتصل" = call again.

reply.english: Great, we'll see each other at 7.
In front of the main entrance.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.english: Lina, where should we meet tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: شو رأيك نلتقي بالمقهى قدام الجامعة؟
dialogue.english: What do you think, shall we meet at the cafe in front of the university?

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.english: Good idea. What time suits you?

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.english: Is 7 o'clock good for you?

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.english: Great, we'll see each other at 7.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.english: Okay, where exactly, in front of the cafe?

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.english: Yes, I'll meet you in front of the main entrance.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.english: Great, I'll definitely be there before you.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.english: Don't be late on me, Lina.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: ولا يهمك، وإذا تأخرت بتصل فيك
dialogue.transliteration: wala yhimmak, w iza ta2akhkharet bittasil fiik
dialogue.english: Don't worry, and if I'm late I'll call you.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.english: Okay, see you tomorrow.

response.english: In front of the main entrance.

pair.english: What do you think, shall we go together?

lessons.culture: Cafes are the default place to arrange to meet in Damascus, and a specific landmark like the Umayyad Mosque or a well-known cafe entrance is given instead of a street address. Confirming the time again by a quick text right before the meeting is normal and expected, not a sign of doubt.

exercises.prompt: A friend asks you: "وين ما نلتقي؟". Suggest meeting at the cafe.

too_formal.feedback: Grammatically correct, but far more formal than a casual suggestion.

exercises.tip: "خلينا" + verb is the everyday way to suggest doing something together.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks: "أي ساعة بتناسبك؟". Say that 7 o'clock is good for you.

too_formal.feedback: Correct but sounds like a written appointment confirmation, not spoken.

exercises.tip: "منيح إلي" is how you say a time "works for me" in Damascene speech.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "بلاقيك _____ المدخل الرئيسي." Meaning: I'll meet you in front of the main entrance.

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but "قدام" is what is actually said in Damascene speech, not "أمام".

exercises.tip: "قدام" means "in front of" in everyday speech.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "إذا _____ اتصل فيي." Meaning: If you're late, call me.

too_formal.feedback: Correct but very formal written Arabic, not how it is said.

exercises.tip: "إذا" + past-tense verb is the everyday conditional in Damascene speech.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Damascene Arabic: "Don't be late."

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but this is a formal written notice style, not spoken Damascene.

exercises.tip: "لا" + present-tense verb is the everyday negative command.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I'll be there before you."

too_formal.feedback: Grammatically identical but uses the formal future "سأ" instead of the spoken "ب".

exercises.tip: "ب" + present-tense verb makes the everyday future in Damascene speech.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence asks "What time suits you?"

too_formal.feedback: Correct but stiffer than the everyday spoken question.

exercises.tip: "بتناسبك" is the spoken form; "يناسبك" alone sounds more formal.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "Let's meet at the cafe"?

too_formal.feedback: Grammatically correct classical form, but not how it's said in conversation.

exercises.tip: "خلينا" + present-tense verb is the everyday "let's" in Damascene speech.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "سبعة / منيح / الساعة".

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but far more elaborate than the short spoken question.

exercises.tip: The time comes first, then the check word "منيح" at the end.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "المدخل الرئيسي / قدام / بلاقيك".

too_formal.item: سألتقي بك أمام المدخل الرئيسي للمبنى
too_formal.feedback: Correct but a much longer, written-style sentence.

exercises.tip: "بلاقيك" (I'll meet you) usually opens the sentence, then the place.

phrases.arabic: مِنِقْدِر نِلْتَقِي بَعِد الظَّهْر بِدَل الصُّبْح؟
phrases.transliteration: mni2dar niltiqi ba3d iḍ-ḍuhur badal iṣ-ṣubu7?

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: آلو سامر، بدي غير موعدنا اليوم
dialogue.transliteration: aaloo Saamer, biddi ghayyir maw3idna l-yoom
dialogue.english: Hello Samer, I want to change our appointment today.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.english: What happened? Is something wrong?

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: إي، طرا علي شغلة بالبيت وما فيني إجي اليوم
dialogue.transliteration: ee, tara 3alay shaghle bil-beet w ma fiini iji l-yoom
dialogue.english: Yeah, something came up at home and I can't come today.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.english: Don't worry about it. Can we postpone to tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: لا مشكلة، منأجل لبكرا. بس منقدر نلتقي بعد الظهر بدل الصبح؟
dialogue.transliteration: la mishkle, mn2ajjil la-bukra. bas mni2dar niltiqi ba3d iḍ-ḍuhur badal iṣ-ṣubu7?
dialogue.english: No problem, we'll postpone to tomorrow. But can we meet in the afternoon instead of the morning?

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: تمام، بعد الظهر أحسن إلي كمان
dialogue.transliteration: tamaam, ba3d iḍ-ḍuhur a7san eli kaman
dialogue.english: Great, the afternoon is better for me too.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.english: Thanks, sorry for the sudden change.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: ولا يهمك، هيك بصير. المكان لسا نفس المكان؟
dialogue.transliteration: wala yhimmak, heek bşiir. il-makaan lissa nafs il-makaan?
dialogue.english: Don't worry, it happens. Is the place still the same place?

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: لأ، غيرنا المكان، منلتقي عند المقهى الجديد
dialogue.transliteration: la2, ghayyarna l-makaan, mniltiqi 3ind il-ma2ha l-jdiid
dialogue.english: No, we changed the place, we'll meet at the new cafe.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: ماشي، بحفظ العنوان. شكرا إنك خبرتيني بدري
dialogue.transliteration: maashi, ba7faẓ il-3inwaan. shukran ennik khabbartiini badri
dialogue.english: Okay, I'll save the address. Thanks for letting me know early.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.english: You're welcome, see you tomorrow afternoon.

pair.english: I want to change the appointment.

pair.arabic: مِنِقْدِر نِلْتَقِي بَعِد الظَّهْر بِدَل الصُّبْح؟
pair.transliteration: mni2dar niltiqi ba3d iḍ-ḍuhur badal iṣ-ṣubu7?
pair.english: Can we meet in the afternoon instead of the morning?

response.english: Yes, the afternoon is better for me.

pair.english: Is the place still the same place?

lessons.culture: Plans change often in daily life in Damascus, and rearranging them on short notice is normal rather than rude, as long as it comes with a quick apology like "آسف عالتغيير المفاجئ". The other person almost always answers with "ولا يهمك" to show there are no hard feelings.

exercises.prompt: Your friend says: "آسف عالتغيير المفاجئ". Tell them not to worry about it.

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but far more formal than the short spoken reassurance.

exercises.tip: "ولا يهمك" is the standard easy way to say "don't worry about it".

exercises.prompt: Someone asks: "ممكن نأجل لبكرا؟". Agree, saying no problem.

too_formal.feedback: Grammatically fine, but this is the written, not the spoken, register.

exercises.tip: "لا مشكلة" is a very common easy agreement phrase.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "_____ علي شغلة وما فيني إجي." Meaning: Something came up for me and I can't come.

too_formal.feedback: Correct but redundant and bookish; the spoken version is much shorter.

exercises.tip: "طرا علي شغلة" is the fixed everyday phrase for "something came up".

exercises.prompt: Complete: "منقدر نلتقي بعد الظهر _____ الصبح؟" Meaning: Can we meet in the afternoon instead of the morning?

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but more formal than the short spoken "بدل" or "عوض".

exercises.tip: "بدل" and "عوض" both mean "instead of" in everyday speech.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Damascene Arabic: "I can't come today."

too_formal.feedback: Grammatically correct but more formal than the everyday spoken phrase.

exercises.tip: "ما فيني" is the everyday "I can't", built from "في + ني".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "Can we postpone to tomorrow?"

too_formal.item: هل يمكننا تأجيل الموعد إلى الغد؟
too_formal.feedback: Correct but a longer, written-style question.

exercises.tip: "ممكن" + present-tense verb is the everyday way to ask "can we...".

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "Is the place still the same place?"

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but more formal phrasing than the spoken question.

exercises.tip: "لسا" means "still" in everyday Damascene speech.

exercises.prompt: Which is a natural apology for changing plans suddenly?

too_formal.item: أعتذر منكم عن هذا التغيير الطارئ
too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but stiff and overly formal for a friend.

exercises.tip: "آسف" (man) / "آسفة" (woman) عالتغيير المفاجئ fits a casual apology.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "لبكرا / نأجل / ممكن".

too_formal.item: هل من الممكن أن نؤجل الأمر إلى الغد
too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but a much longer formal question.

exercises.tip: "ممكن" opens the question, then the verb, then the day.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "الصبح / بدل / بعد الظهر / نلتقي / منقدر".
exercises.answer: منقدر نلتقي بعد الظهر بدل الصبح
accepted: منقدر نلتقي بعد الظهر بدل الصبح

too_formal.item: هل بإمكاننا اللقاء بعد الظهيرة عوضاً عن الصباح؟
too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but a longer, more formal question.

exercises.tip: "منقدر" (can we) opens it, then the verb, then the two times being compared.

reply.english: Sure, what do you want to tell him?

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.english: Hello, is Samer there?

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: لأ، مش هون هلق، طلع عالسوق
dialogue.english: No, he's not here right now, he went out to the market.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.english: Ah, roughly when will he be back?

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: ما بعرف بالضبط، بعد شوي إن شاء الله
dialogue.transliteration: ma ba3ref biḍ-ḍabt, ba3d shwaay in shaa2 alla
dialogue.english: I don't know exactly, in a bit God willing.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.english: Okay, can you take a message for me?

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.english: Sure, what do you want to tell him?

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.arabic: قلها معك رامي اتصل وبدو ياه يرجع يتصل فيي
dialogue.transliteration: 2illa ma3ik Raami ittasal w biddo yaa yirja3 yittasil fiyye
dialogue.english: Tell him Rami called and wants him to call me back.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.english: Okay, I'll tell him as soon as he arrives.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.english: Does he have my number?

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: ما بعرف، خليني آخد رقمك احتياط
dialogue.transliteration: ma ba3ref, khalliini aakhud ra2mak i7tiyaat
dialogue.english: I don't know, let me take your number just in case.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.english: Here you go, thanks a lot for the favor.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: عالرحب والسعة، بترجعلو الخبر أول ما يفوت
dialogue.transliteration: 3ar-ra7b w is-se3a, birja3lo l-khabar awwal ma yfuut
dialogue.english: You're very welcome, I'll pass him the news as soon as he's in.

response.english: No, he's not here right now.
I don't know exactly, in a bit.

pair.english: Can you take a message for me?

response.english: Sure, what do you want to tell him?

lessons.culture: It's normal in Damascus for a family member or roommate to answer the phone and take a message for someone who is out, and a caller is expected to give their name clearly the first time so the message makes sense later. "يسلمو" and "عالرحب والسعة" are the standard thank-you and reply for a favor like taking a message.

exercises.prompt: Someone calling asks: "سامر موجود؟" but he is out. Say he's not here right now.

too_formal.item: لا، إنه غير متواجد في الوقت الحالي
too_formal.feedback: Grammatically correct but sounds like an office receptionist, not a spoken reply.

exercises.tip: "مش هون هلق" is the everyday "not here right now".

exercises.prompt: Someone asks you: "ممكن تاخدلي رسالة؟" Agree and ask what they want to say.

too_formal.item: بالتأكيد، ما الذي تريد أن تخبره به؟
too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but far more formal than the everyday phrasing.

exercises.tip: "شو بدك تقوله" is the natural way to ask what someone wants relayed.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "_____ اتصل فيني." Meaning: Tell him to call me.

too_formal.feedback: Grammatically correct but a written-style instruction, not the short spoken one.

exercises.tip: "قله" is the short spoken form of "tell him".

exercises.prompt: Complete: "بخبره _____ ما يوصل." Meaning: I'll tell him as soon as he arrives.

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but a more formal written order of the sentence.

exercises.tip: "أول ما" is the everyday way to say "as soon as".

exercises.prompt: Translate into Damascene Arabic: "Do you have my number?"

too_formal.feedback: Correct but more formal wording than the short spoken question.

exercises.tip: "عندك" / "معك" both work for "do you have" in everyday speech.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "Thanks a lot."

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but far more formal than the everyday "يسلمو".

exercises.tip: "يسلمو" is one of the most common everyday thank-yous.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence asks "When will he be back?"

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but the formal written question word "متى" instead of the spoken "إمتى".

exercises.tip: "إمتى" is the everyday word for "when".

exercises.prompt: Which is the natural reply to "يسلمو كتير"?

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but a more formal set phrase than the everyday reply.

exercises.tip: "عالرحب والسعة" is the standard easy reply to a thank-you.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "رسالة / تاخدلي / ممكن".

too_formal.item: هل يمكن أن تدوّن لي رسالة؟
too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but a longer, more formal question.

exercises.tip: "ممكن" opens the request, then the verb, then what is being asked for.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "يوصل / ما / أول / بخبره".

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but a longer written-style sentence.

exercises.tip: "بخبره" (I'll tell him) opens it, then the time clause "أول ما يوصل".

challenge.title: A Phone Call to Rearrange Plans
challenge.instructions: Write and act out a phone conversation of at least 10 lines. It must include answering the phone, proposing a place and a time to meet, changing that plan for a real reason, agreeing on a new time or place, and, if the person you called is not free, leaving a message for someone else to pass on.
required_elements: Asking or stating who is calling, using مين معي or معك + name.
A suggestion of where to meet, using خلينا نلتقي or a similar phrase.
A question about time, using أي ساعة بتناسبك or الساعة قديش.
A reason for changing the plan, using طرا علي شغلة or a similar phrase.
A request to postpone or change, using ممكن نأجل or منقدر نلتقي.
An apology for the change, using آسف عالتغيير المفاجئ or a similar phrase.
A reassurance in response, using ولا يهمك.
At least one exchange about leaving or taking a message, using رسالة, قله, or خبره.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.english: Hello?

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: مرحبا سامر، معك لينا. شو الأخبار؟
dialogue.transliteration: mar7aba Saamer, ma3ak Leena. shu l-akhbaar?
dialogue.english: Hi Samer, it's Lina. What's new?

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.english: All good, thank God. What's up?

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: خلينا نلتقي بالمقهى بكرا، أي ساعة بتناسبك؟
dialogue.transliteration: khalliina niltiqi bil-ma2ha bukra, ayy saa3a betnasbak?
dialogue.english: Let's meet at the cafe tomorrow, what time suits you?

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.english: 5 o'clock is good for me.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.english: Great, I'll meet you in front of the main entrance.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: آسف بس، طرا علي شغلة بالبيت وما فيني إجي الساعة خمسة
dialogue.transliteration: aasif bas, tara 3alay shaghle bil-beet w ma fiini iji is-saa3a khamse
dialogue.english: Sorry but, something came up at home and I can't come at 5.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.english: Don't worry about it. Can we postpone to 7?

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: لا مشكلة، منأجل لسبعة. آسف عالتغيير المفاجئ
dialogue.transliteration: la mishkle, mn2ajjil la-sab3a. aasif 3at-taghyiir il-mfaaji2
dialogue.english: No problem, we'll postpone to 7. Sorry for the sudden change.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: ولا يهمك أبدا. بس إذا ما قدرت تيجي، بتقدر تخبر أخوك ياخدلي رسالة
dialogue.transliteration: wala yhimmak abadan. bas iza ma 2dirt tiji, btid2ar tikhbir akhuuk yaakhudli risaale
dialogue.english: Don't worry at all. But if you can't come, you can tell your brother to take a message for me.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.english: Sure, I'll tell him. Thanks a lot for your patience.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.english: You're very welcome, see you at 7.
